records.quote: Fifteen years later, Rosie Briggs stood in the door of it
records.paraphrase: The narrative jumps ahead fifteen years.

records.quote:
her rouged cheeks and scarlet
lips and half-bared heaving breasts contrasted strangely with her
honest eyes.
records.paraphrase: Rosie's dance-hall appearance contrasts with her honest character.

records.quote:
The current of her life had swept past its one clean
tranquil place and was swirling along muddied and normal.
records.paraphrase: Rosie feels her old troubled self returning.

records.quote:
in the midst of cleanness and
silence unbroken since that old rocky backbone of the continent thrust
itself up into the sun, she had risen slowly out of the shards of the
life of Captain Mac and come, late but surely, into her heritage of
womanliness and dignity.
records.paraphrase: Rosie has transformed over the years into a dignified woman.

records.paraphrase: Jim is pained by seeing Rosie drunk.

records.paraphrase: Jim announces he has struck a valuable ore vein.

records.quote:
Whatever
else it meant, it meant the end of this; the beginning of uncertainty.
records.paraphrase: Rosie anticipates the wealth will end their stable life.

records.quote:
And when it cut across the stillness like
the whistle of a locomotive it struck her cold. It chilled the core of
her spirit
records.paraphrase: Rosie feels dread when she realizes Jim has struck ore.

records.quote:
A knife seemed to unfold inside of Rosie. It cut her song off in the
middle of the line and brought her upright in her chair with a gasp.
records.paraphrase: Rosie reacts with sudden dread to smelling perfume on Jim's coat.

records.quote:
They always left the women they had picked up
when they were poor. Especially dance hall women. Even when they were
their wives.
records.paraphrase: Rosie reasons that newly rich miners abandon the poor women who supported them.

records.quote:
By one means and another they made their way into the Gray Dome country
and Jim built a cabin there.
records.paraphrase: The couple relocates to a new place and starts a new life.

criteria.rationale: Mining, ore assay value, and geology appear only as ordinary period realism, not as materially represented scientific facts, theories, or speculative science.
A pick, lamp, banjo, and mine are ordinary contemporary tools; no device or invention functions speculatively or as an engineered novum driving the story.
The fifteen-year jump is ordinary narrative chronology, not a speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement.

Rosie's inferences about newly rich miners abandoning poor women are ordinary social reasoning, not extrapolation from an identifiable scientific, technological, or historical premise in the Knight sense.
No observation, hypothesis, testing, measurement, or evidential revision materially drives understanding; Rosie's perfume suspicion is ordinary intuition, later simply corrected.
The setting is an ordinary terrestrial Colorado mining region; no other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors appear.
The story's crises are personal and emotional; there is no natural, technological, cosmic, biological, or human-caused large-scale disaster, actual or impending.

candidates.description: Jim Briggs's discovery of a rich ore vein ('two hundred dollars to the ton'), which promises sudden wealth and upends the couple's settled life.

novelty.rationale: A mining strike is a mundane event fully consistent with the mining-camp realism of the author's empirical world. It introduces no totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical norm; it is a plausible economic event in a Colorado mining setting.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The strike is coherent, systematic, immanent, and nonsupernatural, grounded in ordinary geology and assaying, but this coherence is that of realism, not of an estranging novum.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The strike is the pivot of the plot: it ends the couple's stable poverty and triggers Rosie's dread and crisis, driving the remaining narrative. However, centrality alone does not make it a novum.

estrangement.rationale: The story offers reader-facing contrast (Rosie's dance-hall appearance vs. honest character) and storyworld change (relocation, time jump, the strike), but these are the ordinary contrasts and turns of a realist regional drama, not cognitive estrangement from an empirical norm. There is no imaginary science or novel social organization structuring the world.
